newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA PARLIAMENT SETS 1997 EXTERNAL DEBT LIMIT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA PARLIAMENT SETS 1997 EXTERNAL DEBT LIMIT.

text.p: The lower chamber of Romanian parliament has set the ceiling of the country's 1997 foreign debt at $3.2 billion, a parliament official said on Tuesday.
"Deputies voted unanimously to approve a government ordinance setting the external debt limit at $3.2 billion for this year," Chamber of Deputies spokesman Horea Popescu said.
In order to become effective the bill has to clear parliament's upper house, the Senate, where the government also relies on a comfortable majority.

The bill entitles Romania's central bank and the finance ministry to raise and guarantee medium- and long-term loans from international capital markets to fund investment, economic restructuring and to enhance hard currency reserves.
Earlier this year National Bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu said his bank plans to raise up to $1.6 billion in 1997.
Virtually absent from world capital markets since the 1980s, Romania resumed activity in 1995 with syndicated loans, followed by its first Samurai and Eurobond issues last year.
It got its first rating from major agencies -- a BB plus from Japan Credit Rating Agency, BB-minus by Standard and Poors and Britain's IBCA and BA-three by Moody's Investors Service.
In 1996 the BNR borrowed around $1.4 billion from world markets and serviced debt payments of around $1.2 billion.
Latest data put Romania's total foreign exchange reserves, including some 88 tonnes of gold, at $3.13 billion at end-1996.
Romania's medium- and long-term external debt was $6.9 billion last year. External debt servicing is estimated at some $1.5 billion in 1997.
